nodes.label: ADR 0020: DiacriticTransfer treats a diphthong as one unit
nodes.rationale: Key lookup and mark transfer are different jobs. normalize_old_english already finds the BT word by stripping marks. BT writes some diphthongs with the macron on the second vowel (eā, eō, iē) while the index's normal style marks the first (ēa, ēo, īe), so a source already marked in one style was double-marked against the other. The transfer treats ea/eo/ie/io as one unit and writes the macron on the first vowel. BTSpellingNormalizer is not used because it rewrites whole strings, is blind to hyphens, and belongs to dictionary parsing. Frontmatter remains proposed; the body says this is implemented in DiacriticTransfer.

nodes.label: DiacriticTransfer
nodes.rationale: Transfer aligns source and reference letter by letter and copies missing marks. mark_pattern is the shared diphthong-canonical helper ADR 0019 uses to compare forms. A hyphen in the reference splits vowels, so be-ōdrian is not the diphthong bēodrian. An unhyphenated prefixed form can hide that boundary and should be reviewed.

nodes.label: normalize_old_english
nodes.rationale: Key lookup lowercases, maps ð to þ, strips every mark, and removes hyphens, so leāst, lēast, and LEAST all resolve to least. Lookup never needs to know where a mark sits, so BTSpellingNormalizer is not part of matching or transfer.

nodes.label: BTSpellingNormalizer
nodes.rationale: The normalizer rewrites whole strings and is blind to hyphens. It belongs to the dictionary-parsing pipeline. Using it for diacritic transfer was rejected because it would solve double-marking only by rewriting strings, and later imports would still need the transfer to accept either diphthong style.

nodes.label: Diphthong treated as one unit
nodes.rationale: A diphthong is an adjacent ea, eo, ie, or io in the reference with no hyphen between the vowels and no mark other than a macron. If the source already marks either vowel, nothing is added; otherwise the reference macron is placed on the first vowel. A breve, as in ēliŏtrŏpus, stays on its own letter because that pair is a hiatus, not a diphthong. The source itself is never rewritten.
